claims.explanation: Fludarabine is a purine nucleoside analog that requires activation by deoxycytidine kinase (DCK) and is inactivated by adenosine deaminase (ADA); its active triphosphate inhibits ribonucleotide reductase (RRM1/RRM2) and DNA polymerase alpha (POLA1), causing DNA synthesis arrest and apoptosis. Selective killing therefore tracks with high DCK expression, low ADA expression, and intact DNA-damage/apoptosis signaling, while TP53 loss and high RRM1/RRM2 or BCL2 expression blunt the response. The strong enrichment of TP53 mutations among sensitive lines is consistent with nucleoside analogs producing replication-associated DNA damage that TP53-mutant cells cannot repair, whereas the resistant lines often retain wild-type TP53 or carry BRAF/PTEN/PIK3CA alterations that support survival.

features.basis: DCK is the rate-limiting activating kinase for fludarabine; high expression increases active triphosphate
ADA deaminates and inactivates fludarabine; high ADA reduces active drug
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, consistent with defective DNA-damage response to nucleoside analog
RRM1 is the fludarabine target ribonucleotide reductase subunit; high expression can overcome inhibition
RRM2 is the other ribonucleotide reductase subunit and a fludarabine target; high expression reduces sensitivity
BCL2 overexpression is a hallmark of CLL and blocks apoptosis downstream of fludarabine-induced damage
POLA1 is a fludarabine target; high expression may buffer polymerase inhibition
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling and appears enriched in resistant lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched in the resistant set, suggesting MAPK-driven survival
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly reflecting oncogene-addicted DNA-replication stress
KRAS-mutant lines are more frequent among resistant lines, consistent with RAS-driven survival signaling
SF3B1-mutant lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly through splicing-induced replication stress
